parsed.main_gap: Justification that at least one entry >1 remains is wrong as stated; needs K drops by at most 1 per move (or product stays >1).

errors.description: The claim that a non-increasing nonnegative integer starting positive can never reach 0 is false in general. The correct (easy) argument: each move replaces two nonunits by gcd and lcm/gcd, at least one of which exceeds 1 (lcm(m,n)>1), so K drops by at most 1, and a move needs K≥2; hence K≥1 always. Straightforward repair, but the written reasoning is invalid.
errors.quote: A nonnegative integer that never increases and starts at a positive value can never reach \(0\); hence \(K\ge1\) at every stage

parsed.notes: Termination via lexicographic (P,K) descent is correct. Choice-independence via prime-wise invariance of gcd of exponents (Euclidean step) is correct and complete, yielding M = prod p^{gcd of v_p}. Only defect is the faulty justification of 'at least one nonunit remains'.
